neighbours.label: One thing physically covering or concealing another: ' over' / ' with' / ' by' / ' cover' where a cloth, mask, blind or layer lies over something
fire: The nurse laid a clean sheet over the patient before the doctor came in.
During the day the skylight can be hidden by a sliding wooden panel.
Wrap the cheese and cover the plate with a sheet of foil.
The rider wore a bandana over the lower half of her face.
Thick ivy covered the wall and most of the garden gate.
He draped his coat over the birdcage so the parrot would sleep.
Long dark hair fell over her eyes as she bent to read.
The statue was concealed by a grey tarpaulin until the ceremony.
quiet: The nurse talked over the plan with the patient before the doctor came in.
During the day the skylight can be opened by a sliding wooden handle.
Slice the cheese and serve the plate with a glass of cider.
The rider won the race over the last half of the course.
The grant covered the fees and most of the travel costs.
He walked over the bridge so the parrot could see the river.
Over the summer her eyes improved and she began to read.
The statue was designed by a young sculptor before the war.

notes: Card: ' cover', ' covered', ' over', and ' by' / ' with' after concealed / cover; the output direction of this pole promotes ' covering', ' veil', ' mask', ' obsc'. Probes: 'a scarf over his mouth' 0.97, 'blanket over the child' 0.76, 'hidden by heavy curtains' 0.69, 'Cover the bowl with a damp cloth' 0.41; 'Over the years' 0.01, 'cover the cost' 0.00, 'jumped over the fence' 0.01, 'written by' 0.01. So it is the covering relation, not the words.
